readings.head: {{RunningHeader|unpalatable|6633|unperishing}}
readings.c1s1:
¶
'''unpalatable''' (un-pal′ā-tạ-bl), ''a.'' Not palatable, in any sense; disagreeable.

'''unpalatably''' (un-pal′ā-tạ-bli), ''adv.'' In an unpalatable manner; disagreeably.

'''unpalped''' (un-palpt′), ''a.'' Having no palpi. ''Claus'', Zoölogy (trans.), p. 470. [Rare.]

'''unpanel''' (un-pan′el), ''v. t.''; pret. and pp. ''unpaneled'', ''unpanelled'', ppr. ''unpaneling'', ''unpanelling''. [< ''un-''<sup>2</sup> + ''panel''.] To take off a panel from; unsaddle. Also spelled ''unpannel''.
{{smaller block|God’s peace be with him who saved us the trouble of ''unpannelling'' Dapple.
{{right|''Jarvis'', tr. of Don Quixote, I. iii. 11. (''Davies''.)}}}}

'''unpanged''' (un-pangd′), ''a.'' Not afflicted with pangs; not pained. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|<poem>We come unseasonably; but when could Grief
Cull forth, as ''unpang’d'' Judgment can, fitt’st time
For best solicitation?</poem>
{{right|''Fletcher'' (''and another''), Two Noble Kinsmen, i. 1.}}}}

'''unparadise''' (un-par′ạ-dīs), ''v. t.'' [< ''un-''<sup>2</sup> + ''paradise''.] To deprive of happiness like that of paradise; render unhappy. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|<poem>Ghastly thought would drink up all your joy,
And quite ''unparadise'' the realms of light.</poem>
{{right|''Young'', Night Thoughts, i.}}}}

'''unparagoned''' (un-par′ạ-gond), ''a.'' Unequaled; unmatched; matchless; peerless.
{{smaller block|Your ''unparagoned'' mistress. ''Shak.'', Cymbeline, i. 4. 87.}}

'''unparallelable''' (un-par′ạ-lel-ạ-bl), ''a.'' Incapable of being paralleled.
{{smaller block|My ''unparallelable'' love to mankind.
{{right|''Bp. Hall'', Mystery of Godliness, vi.}}}}
readings.c1s2:
¶
'''unparalleled''' (un-par′a̤-leld), ''a.'' Having no parallel or equal; unequaled; unmatched.
{{smaller block|<poem>The elder Cretans flourish’d many years,
In war, in peace ''unparallel’d.''</poem>
{{right|''Beau. and Fl.'', Laws of Candy, i. 1.}}}}

'''unparasitized''' (un-par′a̤-sī-tīzd), ''a.'' Not infested, or unaffected, by a parasite.

'''unpardonable''' (un-pär′do̤n-a-bl), ''a.'' Not to be forgiven; incapable of being pardoned or remitted: as, an ''unpardonable'' insult.
{{smaller block|’Tis a fault too too ''unpardonable.''
{{right|''Shak.'', 3 Hen. VI., i. 4. 106.}}}}

'''Unpardonable sin''', {{smaller|the sin of blasphemy against the Holy Ghost (Mat. xii. 31). See ''blasphemy''.}}

'''unpardonableness''' (un-pär′do̤n-a-bl-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unpardonable.

'''unpardonably''' (un-pär′do̤n-a-bli), ''adv.'' Not in a pardonable manner or degree; beyond pardon or forgiveness.

'''unparegal†''', ''a.'' [Also ''unperegal''; < ME. ''unparegal'', ''unparygal''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''paregal''.] Unequal.
readings.c1s4:
¶
'''unpassable''' (un-pȧs′a̤-bl), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not admitting passage; impassable.
{{smaller block|But seeing these North-easterne Seas are so frozen and ''vnpassable.''
{{right|''Purchas'', Pilgrimage, p. 435.}}}}
'''2.''' Not current; not received in common payments; uncurrent: as, ''unpassable'' notes or coins.
{{smaller block|Making a new standard for money must make all money which is lighter than that standard ''unpassable.''
{{right|''Locke''}}}}
readings.c2s1:
¶
'''unpassableness''' (un-pȧs′a̤-bl-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unpassable.
{{smaller block|Grave authors, who speak of the ''unpassibleness'' of the ocean, mention the worlds that lay beyond it.
{{right|''Evelyn'', Navigation and Commerce.}}}}

'''unpassionate''' (un-pash′o̤n-āt), ''a.'' '''1.''' Free from bias; impartial; dispassionate.
{{smaller block|This coole ''unpassionate'' mildnesse of positive wisdome is not enough to damp and astonish the proud resistance of carnal and false Doctors.
{{right|''Milton'', Apology for Smectymnuus.}}}}
'''2.''' Not exhibiting passion or strong emotion; especially, not angry.
{{smaller block|Sober, grave, and ''unpassionate'' words.
{{right|''Locke'', Thoughts on Education.}}}}

'''unpassionated†''' (un-pash′o̤n-ā-ted), ''a.'' Dispassionate. ''Glanville'', Vanity of Dogmatizing, xi.

'''unpassionately''' (un-pash′o̤n-āt-li), ''adv.'' Dispassionately; impartially; calmly. ''Eikon Basilike.''

'''unpassioned''' (un-pash′o̤nd), ''a.'' Free from passion; dispassionate. ''Sir J. Davies'', Witte’s Pilgrimage, p. 48.

'''unpastor†''' (un-pȧs′tor), ''v. t.'' [< ''un-''<sup>2</sup> + ''pastor.''] To deprive of the office of a pastor; cause to be no longer a pastor. ''Fuller.''

'''unpathed''' (un-pätht′), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''path'' + ''-ed''<sup>2</sup>.] Having no paths; pathless; trackless. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|<poem>A wild dedication of yourselves
To ''unpath’d'' waters.</poem>{{right|''Shak.'', W. T., iv. 4. 578.}}}}

'''unpathwayed''' (un-päth′wād), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''pathway'' + ''-ed''<sup>2</sup>.] Having no pathway; pathless; unpathed. [Rare.]
readings.c2s2:
{{smaller block|<poem>She roves through St. John’s Vale
Along the smooth ''unpathwayed'' plain.</poem>
{{right|''Wordsworth'', The Waggoner, iv. 24.}}}}

'''unpatience†''' (un-pā′shens), ''n.'' [< ME. ''unpacience''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''patience''.] Impatience.
{{smaller block|<poem>''Unpacience''
Causede me to don offence.</poem>
{{right|''Rom. of the Rose'', l. 4575.}}}}

'''unpatient†''' (un-pā′shent), ''a.'' [< ME. ''unpacient''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''patient''.] Impatient.
{{smaller block|''Vnpacient'' in alle penaunces and pleyned, as hit were, On god, whenne me greued ouht and grucched of hus sonde.
{{right|''Piers Plowman'' (C), vii. 110.}}}}

'''unpatriotic''' (un-pā-tri-ot′ik), ''a.'' Not patriotic. ''Quarterly Rev.''

'''unpatronized''' (un-pā′trọn-īzd), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not having a patron; not supported by friends. ''Johnson'', Rambler, No. 120.—'''2.''' Not traded with customarily; not frequented by customers: as, an ''unpatronized'' dealer or shop. [Commercial cant.]

'''unpatterned''' (un-pat′ėrnd), ''a.'' Having no pattern; unequaled; peerless.
{{smaller block|Should I prize you less, ''unpattern’d'' Sir.
{{right|''Beau. and Fl.'', Thierry and Theodoret, iii.}}}}

'''unpaved''' (un-pāvd′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not paved; not covered with stone.
{{smaller block|Streets, which were for the most part ''unpaved.''
{{right|''The American'', VI. 281.}}}}
'''2†.''' Castrated; gelded. ''Shak.'', Cymbeline, ii. 3. 34. [Ludicrous.]

'''unpay†''' (un-pā′), ''v. t.'' [< ''un-''<sup>2</sup> + ''pay''<sup>1</sup>.] To undo; annul by payment. [Humorous.]

Imperfection. {{smaller block|Being of my ''unperfectness'' unworthy of your friendship.{{right|''Sir P. Sidney'', Arcadia, i.}}}} '''unperformed''' (un-pėr-fôrmd′), ''a.'' Not performed; not done; not executed; not fulfilled; hence, not represented on the stage; unacted: as, the business remains ''unperformed''; an ''unperformed'' promise; the play remained ''unperformed.'' {{smaller block|This voyage, ''unperform’d'' by living man.{{right|''Cowper'', Odyssey, x.}}}} '''unperishable†''' (un-per′ish-a-bl), ''a.'' Not perishable; imperishable. ''Spectator'', No. 537. '''unperishably†''' (un-per′ish-ạ-bli), ''adv.'' Imperishably. '''unperishing''' (un-per′ish-ing), ''a.'' Not perishing; lasting; durable. {{smaller block|Her great sire’s ''unperishing'' abode.{{right|''Cowper'', Iliad, xix.}}}}
